Hi Anita — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the items we discussed for procurement/billing so your team can move this forward:

- Demo recap: We showed Redwood hosted inference, dedicated capacity options, and the cost/latency tradeoffs for your LLM workloads.
- Next commercial steps we discussed: procurement path (PO vs. card), invoicing requirements, net terms, and marketplace interest (AWS Marketplace).

Action items / questions for procurement (so we have everything to create a quote & legal):
1) Preferred payment path: PO (standard for you) or corporate card?
2) Standard net terms requested (Net 30/Net 45)? Any approvals needed?
3) Billing address and remit-to address to appear on invoice.
4) Tax/VAT requirements: do you require Redwood to include VAT or provide any tax forms (VAT ID / tax exemption)?
5) Invoice format: PDF with itemized line items ok? Do you need electronic invoice ingestion (XML/EDI)?
6) Marketplace interest: would you prefer to procure via AWS Marketplace (Redwood supports marketplace billing) or direct vendor invoice? Marketplace changes procurement flow and contract model, so let us know preference.

Attached: Redwood_Invoice_Template.xlsx (template of our invoice fields) and Redwood_SOW_Template.pdf for scope/initial term assumptions. Also including our W-9 in the next email.

If you can confirm answers to 1–5 and share any vendor onboarding forms, we can hand this to our Billing/Ops to draft the invoice and prepare the PO-ready paperwork.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with our Billing ops (cc’d) to speed vendor registration.

Best,

Hi Anita — great questions. Answers below and next steps from our side:

1) PO vs Card / Net terms
- We support both PO and corporate card. For enterprise customers PO + invoice is the standard flow.
- Our standard payment terms are Net 30. Net 45 or custom terms can be approved via commercial exceptions (requires sign-off from finance) — we can surface that if needed.

2) Invoice format / electronic ingestion
- We can produce PDF invoices with itemized line items (standard).
- We also support CSV/XML invoice exports and can push to SFTP/EDI for enterprise invoice ingestion — please let us know the transport method and sample spec and our Billing Ops will validate.

3) Tax / VAT
- Redwood is a US company; for US entity purchases we’ll include our US tax ID on the invoice.
- For EU VAT requirements, our Billing Ops can issue VAT invoices when required (we support VAT registration workflows for customers in scope).

4) Required invoice fields (so your AP team has everything):
- Invoice number
- Invoice date
- PO number (if applicable)
- Bill-to name & billing address
- Remit-to / payment instructions
- Line-item description, quantity, unit price, extended amount
- Redwood tax ID / VAT ID (as applicable)
- Contact for invoice questions (billing@redwoodinference.com)

5) Marketplace billing
- We do support AWS Marketplace. Note this changes the contracting and billing cadence (Marketplace buys often go through the marketplace billing pipeline and may have different refund/termination terms). Consolidated monthly billing across multiple AWS Marketplace SKUs is possible, but we’ll confirm specifics with our marketplace team if you opt for that route.

Attachments: I’ve attached our Redwood_Invoice_Template.xlsx and a copy of our W-9 (Redwood_W9.pdf) to speed vendor onboarding. Laura (cc’d) is our Head of Billing Ops; she can pick up vendor registration items and confirm format specs.

Next steps: If you confirm PO path and provide billing address & PO template (if any), Laura will send a vendor setup packet and draft the first invoice. Alternatively, if you prefer card or marketplace, let us know and we’ll route accordingly.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with procurement if that speeds things up.

Best,
Marissa
